findings.instruction_sentence: Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.
findings.departure: Input class: a presented signature padded with something other than ASCII space (tab, CR/LF, NBSP U+00A0). h3 seq 1 pads with plain spaces only. Reading 1 (oracle, String.prototype.trim): all Unicode whitespace stripped, verified. Reading 2: only spaces and tabs are 'whitespace' (e.g. the folding regex /[ \t]/ the canonical rule already uses), so NBSP or CRLF padding is a signature-mismatch. Both reproduce all 8 graded sets. Example value is `signature= <good> `.

findings.departure: Input class: an x-gw-key-id value with surrounding whitespace (` gw-prod-01 `). This decides the keyId binding, since the prefix is built from the record key id. Reading 1 (oracle headerOf/headerValue): the value is trimmed, key_id is `gw-prod-01`, the header's `keyId=gw-prod-01` binds, verified. Reading 2: used verbatim, key_id carries the spaces, unknown-key-id with empty signature. The dossier register (01-decision-register.md line 92, 'the value itself is used verbatim') supports reading 2, so the oracle departs from the dossier here as well; instruction.md is silent. No graded key id has surrounding whitespace. Borderline with the keys lens, reported because it changes the keyId binding.

findings.instruction_sentence: `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`
findings.departure: JSON key order. instruction.md says 'Every evidence object has exactly these keys' and lists them, but never states that the keys must be serialised in that order; an agent that emits `reason` right after `outcome` (a natural grouping) produces the same key set, passes test_evidence_is_valid_ndjson, and fails every byte comparison: base sample seq 4,5,7,8; h1 seq 3; h2 seq 2,3; h3 seq 2,3,4,5,6 (hard likewise plus h1 seq 7, h2 seq 5). The starter /app/src/pipeline.ts emits only seq,key_id,method,outcome,signature, so it does not fix the order of the keys the agent must add. Borderline: the list order is a strong implicit cue, so severity low.
findings.other_tests_checked: test_evidence_is_valid_ndjson passes (same key set); test_verification_outcomes_are_correct passes (same values); only the sha256 byte comparisons fail, on every set containing a rejected record.
